cases.why: a gap of zero is treated as a lead, so a tie at the top prints 'leads by 0 games' -- a headline that picks a winner the numbers did not.
a one-game lead reads 'leads by 1 games', in the largest type on the page.
the bars start at the coin-flip line instead of zero, so 68.8% against 71.9% draws a bar 14% shorter than the leader's instead of 4% -- the gap of one game, more than tripled.
the equal-count check goes, so records over different sets of games get a margin in games, which is not a like-for-like difference.
cases.find: if(!sameGames) return `${lead} has the best record so far.`;
